Team — high level tax guidance for Colombia (non-exhaustive):

- Domestic vs. non-resident: If ServiCol is a Colombia tax resident (RUT active) and supplies services locally, standard VAT (IVA) rules could apply; for services rendered to a non-resident, VAT may not be charged but DIAN treatments vary. From the documents provided, ServiCol is domestic (has RUT) so VAT may be on their invoices where applicable.
- Withholding (retención en la fuente): For payments to local suppliers, withholding rates depend on the payment concept. For services performed in Colombia, common rates: 11% (services without VAT) or 3.5% (professional services) — we must map the invoice concept to the code used in our AP engine.
- For cross-border payments to non-residents, different treaty/withholding rules apply: need residency determination. Since ServiCol is Colombian-resident, Redwood should NOT gross-up for Colombian WHT: we withhold at source where required and provide a retenido comprobante to vendor.

Action items for Ben:
- Receive ServiCol withholding matrix and confirm mapping to our AP codes (I will review the attached XLSX).
- Confirm whether Redwood can accept XML with a <Withholding> tag or whether we need a separate retenido PDF attached.

I will review the XML schema this afternoon and return a short checklist. If retention is required, we will deduct at payment time and issue a retention certificate (form 220).

-ben
Ben Carter
Tax & Treasury Manager | Redwood Inference

Hello Redwood team,

We are the certified provider for ServiCol. Quick technical clarifications: 

- Feed options: we support (1) SFTP drop with filename convention (NIT_invoiceNumber.xml), (2) HTTPS POST with multipart (xml + pdf), or (3) AS2. For automated AP ingestion our customers typically use SFTP + nightly poll.
- Schema: we publish FACTURA-E UBL 2.1 variant used in Colombia. Our sample XML (attached by ServiCol) includes a <Retencion> block which contains the DIAN retenido metadata. If Redwood wants the retenido as a separate PDF, we can emit it as an attachment under the same envelope.
- Testing: we provide a sandbox endpoint and IMS test certificates. To complete the test we need Redwood to: (A) confirm SFTP creds or HTTPS endpoint, (B) provide expected filename pattern, (C) run a draft invoice through the sandbox and confirm parsing.
